Do you have to buy Apple's largest iPhone Pro to get the best camera features? The answer has varied over the years. Until now, most reports have suggested there will be no camera specification differences between the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, but today a leaker has cast some doubt on that claim.

Specifically, they say that two new features originally expected to appear on both Pro models will "probably" be exclusive to the Pro Max only…

The iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max offer identical camera specs, with all three rear lenses featuring 48-megapixel sensors. Apple states the telephoto lens can achieve up to 8x optical zoom, but this is achieved by cropping a 24-megapixel image, so it would be more accurate to say it has 4x optical zoom with the option to crop to 8x.

We currently (basically) expect this year's Pro models to maintain parity in camera specs, with both featuring a variable aperture main lens and a telephoto lens with a wider aperture, the latter enabling better low-light performance.

However, leaker Ice Universe says these two new telephoto lens features may be exclusive to the iPhone 18 Pro Max only.

If true, this means if you want the longest telephoto reach and the best low-light performance, you'll have to go for the Pro Max. However, the use of "probably" suggests they're not entirely sure of this claim, perhaps because they've seen conflicting evidence within Apple's supply chain.

Some have also suggested that the variable aperture system for the main lens may be exclusive to the Pro Max only, but there are differing opinions on this as well.

If you usually prefer the smaller of the two Pro models, would you upgrade to the Pro Max for the better camera features? Let us know in the comments.
